summary:
• Meta's Muse Wonder — Meta's second‑generation frontier language model, offering fast and full‑scale tiers with 1 M token context for high‑throughput personal‑agent applications.
• Folkbench — An open‑source Tauri‑based desktop client that lets users switch between AI API endpoints instantly, displaying latency, token usage and cost to optimise performance.
• Codex CLI — A command‑line tool now bundled with a background daemon that auto‑updates, which can continue running after the terminal closes, potentially creating unwanted processes.
• Web‑edit — A lightweight Python web app using CodeMirror that serves a folder over Tailscale, enabling secure mobile editing of files without exposing data to external services.
• New‑Term‑Radar — A daily scraper that monitors early mentions of AI‑related terms across social platforms and surfaces emerging names before traditional keyword tools detect them.
• Local AI — Running large language models on personal hardware, now feasible with Apple’s Mac Studio, RTX Spark GPUs and open‑source models like Hermes for private, on‑device assistants.
